Hello,

I am considering purchasing either the Harlo B30 or the Nexus S1, and before placing an order I would like to clarify the actual power consumption and efficiency of both models.

Regarding the Harlo B30, I understand that it is normally rated at around 30 TH/s and approximately 360–450 W.

Does the B30 currently have an officially supported low-power / efficiency mode available directly in Harlo OS, without custom firmware or unofficial modifications?

If so, could you please confirm:

The available low-power profiles or settings.
The expected hashrate for each profile.
The actual AC wall power consumption, including the PSU.
Whether it is possible to operate the B30 continuously at approximately 150–200 W, and what hashrate I should realistically expect at that power level.
Whether using the official low-power settings has any effect on the warranty or RMA coverage.

I would also like to clarify the specifications of the Nexus S1 with 4× BM1373 chips.

I have seen different power figures associated with this model: some information mentions approximately 100 W at around 10 TH/s, while the current product page appears to indicate approximately 150 W.

Could you please confirm:

Whether the Nexus S1 you currently sell is still the 4× BM1373 version.
Its actual sustained hashrate at the standard factory setting.
Its actual AC wall power consumption including the supplied PSU at that setting.
Whether approximately 100–110 W at around 10 TH/s is achievable on the current production unit using an officially supported efficiency profile, without aggressive undervolting, overclocking, or warranty-affecting modifications.
If 100 W is not realistic, what wall power should I expect during continuous normal operation.

My priority is not maximum hashrate. I am specifically looking for a multi-BM1373 miner that can run efficiently and conservatively for long periods, ideally at no more than about 200 W total.

Thank you very much.
Handed to the team · detailed power/efficiency specs not in the product data

That's a good, precise list, and it's now with the person who answers the hardware.

What I can confirm from the listing: the Nexus S1 we sell is 4× BM1373, ~10 TH/s at ~150W, ~15 J/TH. The B30 is ~30 TH/s at 360–450W. The rest, the low-power profiles, real wall watts and the warranty question, I won't guess at.
